summary: SLA escalation flows misrouted after routing rules refresh; macros failing in console and weekly SLA report mismatch
description:
Issue summary:
A scheduled refresh of support routing rules (auto-deploy triggered 2026-03-10 02:15 UTC) caused SLA escalation flows to route to the wrong queue and a subset of support macros used by Tier 1 agents to auto-populate escalation fields began returning 500 errors. The weekly SLA calculation job produced a mismatch relative to the prior baseline (delta ~2.8% on 'first response within SLA') after the refresh.

Impact:
- Escalation alerts routed to 'Platform On-Call' instead of 'Support Escalations' for ~90 tickets between 02:20–02:55 UTC.
- Tier 1 agents reported 500 errors when invoking escalation macros in the console, causing manual processing and delayed responses.
- Weekly SLA report shows a 2.8% regression for first-response SLA for us-east prod support dataset; the regression window aligns with routing refresh.

Environment:
- support-tooling: prod cluster (us-east), routing service v2026-03-10-2 (auto-refreshed), sla-engine v1.14.3, console v4.7.0.

Steps to reproduce (observed sequence):
1) Auto-refresh job applied routing rule set v2026-03-10-2 at 2026-03-10 02:15 UTC.
2) Incoming escalations processed through new rules and matched a new priority-condition that routes to the legacy platform queue.
3) Console escalation macro call to /api/internal/macros/escalate returned 500 with stacktrace referencing routing module NPE.
4) SLA calculation job (weekly-runner) aggregated event stream and reported increased misses for first-response SLA.

Observed behavior:
- Wrong queue assignment for escalations (Platform instead of Support Escalations).
- Macros failing with 500 errors until manual retries were attempted.
- SLA reporting shows a spike in SLA misses coincident with the window.

Expected behavior:
- Routing refresh should preserve escalation routing mappings and pass unit validations.
- Macros should execute without 500s; proper error handling should surface non-fatal warnings.
- Weekly SLA report should remain consistent or indicate only true changes.

Temporary workaround applied:
- At 2026-03-10 03:10 UTC, routing refresh roll-back to v2026-03-09-7 performed (pins routing to previous stable rules).
- Disabled routing auto-refresh job until root cause identified.
steps_to_reproduce: Trigger auto-refresh of routing rules using scheduled job (simulate v2026-03-10-2)
Send test escalation payload matching priority-condition used in incident window
Call console macro /api/internal/macros/escalate and observe response code
Run weekly SLA aggregator on event sample spanning 02:00–04:00 UTC and compare first-response rates
logs_snippets: 2026-03-10T02:23:11Z ERROR console.macros - 500 POST /api/internal/macros/escalate  -> java.lang.NullPointerException: missing escalation_target
2026-03-10T03:05:02Z INFO scheduler - Rollback to routing version v2026-03-09-7 initiated by ops_runbook
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: a regression in routing rule schema parsing allowed a new condition to evaluate true for legacy platform queue (confirmed by rule diff between v2026-03-09-7 and v2026-03-10-2)
Reproduced NPE locally when a routing rule included an empty 'escalation_target' field; parser didn't validate presence of required keys (unit tests did not cover absent escalation_target case)
Macros bubble up the routing NPE because they call routing.match() synchronously; lack of defensive null checks in routing module propagated 500 to console layer
SLA aggregator rerun on archived event stream (post-rollback) shows metrics returned to baseline for sampled set (preliminary)
next_steps: Add defensive validation in routing parser to reject rule sets with missing escalation_target (PR in support-tooling repo)
Add unit + integration tests for rule schema edge cases and macro failure scenarios
Coordinate with Release Engineering to harden auto-refresh gating: add schema validation and canary rollout to 10% before global refresh
Re-run full weekly SLA job for us-east after fixes and validate with data engineering
related_actions: Hotfix rolled: console macro layer added try/catch to surface user-friendly error while upstream routing is validated
resolution: Investigating. Temporary rollback to routing version v2026-03-09-7 and auto-refresh disabled. Hotfix applied to console macros to prevent uncaught NPEs. Routing schema validation PR open and assigned to platform team. Awaiting test results and full SLA re-run before closing.
